name: Fexofenadine
route_note: Oral tablet or suspension once or twice daily, with water rather than fruit juice
originator: Hoechst Marion Roussel (from work at Georgetown University and Sepracor)
owner: generic (many); Allegra brand: Opella (Sanofi consumer health)

discovery.by: Researchers including Raymond Woosley at Georgetown University
discovery.note: Identified as the active, non-cardiotoxic carboxylic-acid metabolite of terfenadine.

rx_status: OTC in the US and many other countries
tagline: Non-sedating antihistamine developed as the safe metabolite of terfenadine
summary: Fexofenadine is the active metabolite of terfenadine, an antihistamine withdrawn because of fatal heart-rhythm problems. It provides the antihistamine effect without terfenadine's QT liability and causes very little sedation.
mechanism: Fexofenadine is a selective inverse agonist at peripheral H1 receptors, inhibiting histamine-induced sneezing, rhinorrhoea, itch and wheal-and-flare responses.

It is a P-glycoprotein substrate and is effectively excluded from the brain, explaining its lack of sedation. Unlike terfenadine, it does not block cardiac hERG potassium channels at therapeutic concentrations.

history.title: Terfenadine
history.detail: Terfenadine (Seldane) is approved in the US; reports of torsades de pointes with interacting drugs follow.

history.title: Terfenadine withdrawal
history.detail: FDA proposes withdrawal of terfenadine, citing fexofenadine as a safer alternative; it leaves the US market in 1998.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic fexofenadine becomes available in the US.

history.title: OTC
history.detail: Allegra switches to over-the-counter status in the US.

pk.metabolism: Minimal (~5%); transported by P-gp and OATP

facts: Grapefruit, orange and apple juice can reduce fexofenadine absorption by inhibiting OATP transporters.
Fexofenadine is a textbook example of developing an active metabolite to avoid the toxicity of a parent drug.
